Uultis / Digital visual systemStyle Guide · 2026

The shape of
a feeling.

Color, type, space and motion. A shared vocabulary that brings the Uultis essence to every detail of the digital experience.

Observed identity. The logo, colors and typographic references SuisseIntl and Athelas, observed in official Uultis channels, are the starting point.

Proposed system. The public version uses open-license Inter and Libre Baskerville, with warm tones, components and motion developed for this redesign. This guide is a project reference and does not replace the institutional brand manual.

Color lets
the material speak.

Neutrals that welcome photography. Contrast that organizes reading. Click any swatch to copy its hexadecimal code.

Foundation observed on the original website

Colors taken from the official Brazilian CSS .

The digital extension

Tones proposed for this project, inspired by wood, textiles and the light in the photographs.

The sage gray #D1D4CC also remains in the digital system. Light tones serve backgrounds and dividers; essential information uses higher contrast. Photography brings color variation.

Consistency begins in the details. Color names connect the guide to the website tokens. Cream and ink form the main pairing; other colors support the composition.

a language.

FLEXIBLE GRID04 COLUMNS
GENEROUS MARGINS · CONSISTENT ALIGNMENT

The website's main side margin starts at 5.1vw. The catalog uses a flexible grid; the editorial narrative can span columns and alternate proportions.

Desktop

Large images, more columns and room to bring detail and context together. Content keeps a comfortable reading width.

Photography + space + contrast

Tablet

Fewer columns, clear navigation and controls within reach. Hierarchy follows the new width without losing its rhythm.

Rearrange, preserve the intent

Mobile

A vertical narrative. Readable products in one or two columns, tailored crops and enough space for every tap.

Content first, natural gestures

06 /

Motion
has its own timing.

Gentle transitions follow the eye. Scrolling stays natural and content remains available with reduced motion.

EDITORIAL REVEAL

Arrive lightly.
Stay with presence.

The reveal combines opacity with a short movement. Gradual deceleration brings the motion to a natural finish.

28PX OF MOVEMENT
1.2SECONDS
Ease outDECELERATION

The demonstration respects the device's motion preference.

Immediate response

Button and control states: around 200–400 ms. Feedback should be perceptible without feeling delayed.

Editorial presence

Photography and content entrances: around 600–1,200 ms. Animation accompanies the composition and then ends.

Freedom of movement

No scroll hijacking. Restrained parallax, video started by the visitor and a static alternative for reduced motion.

07 /

Beauty is also
found in care.

The visual standard is complete when the experience is readable, navigable and comfortable across screens and input methods.

01

Reading with contrast

Primary text in ink on cream. Light grays belong on surfaces. Essential information never relies on color alone.

02

Visible focus

Links and controls keep visible keyboard outlines. Navigation order follows reading order and a skip link leads to content.

03

A comfortable tap

Interactive icons use targets of at least 44 × 44 px. The drawing can be delicate while the touch target stays generous.

04

Thoughtful image delivery

Images with defined dimensions reduce layout shifts. The opening image takes priority; offscreen images load on demand.

05

Faithful content

Names, credits and descriptions preserve their sources. Each piece links to its official page, technical sheet and 3D model where available.

06

Motion by choice

Reduced-motion preferences disable long animations. Text and static images keep the experience understandable.

These guidelines document the system's intent and choices. Accessibility review should accompany each new component and content item, including contrast, keyboard access and small-screen readability.
